relevance_note: Case report of a girl with PAPA syndrome and an osteolytic lesion: "The molecular analysis of PSTPIP1 gene revealed the E250Q pathogenic mutation 1 in both the patient and the father".
method_note: Read the paper by hand; no tables. Three people: the index girl ('patient', rule 5), her father ('father of patient', rule 2; carrier with severe acne), and one previously published PAPA patient from Demidowich et al (reference 3) given an individual-level feature (osteomyelitis), labelled 'ref 3 patient' under the v4 passing-mention rule; no variant is printed for that person, so no variant row. The variant is printed only as the protein shorthand 'E250Q' (no p. prefix, no cDNA, no transcript); recorded as printed in protein_hgvs_as_stated. Zygosity is not stated (only 'autosomal dominant condition' about the disease in general), so not reported. Inheritance for the patient recorded as inherited paternal because the father carries the same variant; maternal testing not reported. Variant type (missense) is not stated by the authors, so not reported. n_patients_reported left null: the authors give no number (two carriers named: patient and father). Age at last evaluation not recorded: the only ages stated are onset (18 months) and referral (33 months); follow-up is given as 'After 6 months' of anakinra without an age. Post-treatment normalization of acute-phase reactants and a negative whole-body MRI after 6 months of anakinra are treated as response to treatment, not as excluded features (summarized in treatment_summary). Biopsy and marrow results negative for malignancy, histiocytosis and tuberculosis recorded as excluded features in the paper's terms. The 'ref 3 patient' checklist item 'sterile osteomyelitis or osteolytic bone lesions' left not reported because the paper says only 'an osteomyelitis' without stating it was sterile or osteolytic. The PAPA disease label is stated for the patient's diagnosis; no diagnosis is stated for the father. No contradictions found.

treatment_summary.value: intravenous antibiotic therapy (temporary partial improvement); nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drug (poor response); prednisone 1 mg/kg/day (prompt good response, recurrence of bone pain at discontinuation); intraarticular triamcinolone hexacetonide (arthritis resolved); anakinra (good control of bone pain and arthritis; acute-phase reactants normalized and MRI negative for osteolytic lesions after 6 months)
span: The girl was treated with intravenous antibiotic therapy with a temporary partial improvement
Nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drug treatment was started, with poor response.
prednisone 1 mg/kg/day was started with a prompt good response, but the recurrence of bone pain at steroid discontinuation
The arthritis completely resolved after an intraarticular injection of triamcinolone hexacetonide.

Treatment with recombinant interleukin 1 (IL-1) receptor antagonist (anakinra) was started with a good control of bone pain and arthritis in the following months. After 6 months, acute-phase reactants normalized and the whole-body MRI was negative for osteolytic bone lesions.

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: Suspected on family history (severe acne in the father); confirmed by molecular analysis of PSTPIP1 showing E250Q in patient and father (earlier diagnosis of CRMO)
span: The careful evaluation of family history revealed the presence of severe acne in the father since adolescence. On this basis, a PAPA (pyogenic arthritis, pyoderma gangrenosum, and acne) syndrome was suspected.
The molecular analysis of PSTPIP1 gene revealed the E250Q pathogenic mutation 1 in both the patient and the father, confirming the final diagnosis.
A diagnosis of chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis (CRMO) was made
